verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own documented self-hosting lets you run the app and its MongoDB on your own infrastructure, so you decide where the data lives. A hands-on probe confirmed a working self-host roundtrip. Its warehouse-native design also keeps experiment data in your own warehouse. Missing for 10: selectable region or residency for GrowthBook Cloud (e.g., EU/US hosting), formal data-residency documentation or guarantees, and independent corroboration of residency controls.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can choose where my data is stored (region/residency)

citations.quote: Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Warehouse Native. Query 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks.
The actual values of targeting attributes (e.g., user IDs, emails) are never sent to GrowthBook. They are only stored in memory locally within the SDK.
so they keep one high-quality data source and avoid sending data to third parties.
